assigned.title: A CI step that hangs reports 'in progress' for six hours instead of failing
assigned.acceptance:
REQUIRED: the jobs in ci.yml and windows.yml get `timeout-minutes`, per step where a step has a credible hang and per job otherwise. THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE. PL-0735 fixes the one step that hangs today; this makes the NEXT one visible. A step with no bound burns GitHub's six-hour default and reports 'in progress' the entire time -- indistinguishable, to the only readable channel this project has (annotations, because job logs need a login), from a runner that is merely queued. That is how CI #181 and #182 both sat unfinished without anyone treating it as a failure.

REQUIRED: each bound is derived from an OBSERVED duration and the derivation is written beside it. A number somebody felt was generous is a number somebody will raise the first time it fires. Observed today: e2e 5m 8s, e2e-typecheck 12s, and the Windows e2e-desktop job 3m 25s.

REQUIRED: the bound is not so tight that a slow runner reads as a defect. A timeout that fires on a cold cache teaches people to re-run rather than to read, which costs more than the hang.

OUT OF SCOPE: the control-plane performance work, which is PL-0735, and any change to what the steps do.
assigned.notes:
SPLIT OUT OF PL-0735 in round 112, carrying its clause verbatim. PL-0735 was filed holding ci.yml and `ai:claim` refused it on an overlap with PL-0728, which is in REVIEW for the rest of the round. Keeping both halves in one task meant neither landed; this one is BACKLOG until ci.yml frees.

Classification C (workflow/harness defect) under the round-112 directive's A-E scheme, same as PL-0735. P1 rather than P0 because PL-0735 removes the hang that exists; this prevents the one that does not exist yet.

assigned.title: Every msiexec call in the lifecycle harness can wait forever
assigned.acceptance:
FOUND BY PL-0736 WHILE BOUNDING THE STEP THAT CONTAINS IT. `lifecycle.mjs` calls `spawnSync("msiexec.exe", args, { encoding: "utf8", windowsHide: true })` four times -- install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall -- and passes no `timeout`. Windows Installer serialises on the `_MSIExecute` mutex and a holder makes the next invocation WAIT rather than fail, so there is no deadline anywhere in the chain that decides F1, F3 and F4.

PL-0736 put a 15-minute `timeout-minutes` on the step. That is an OUTER bound and deliberately not the fix: when it fires, the whole step dies and the report says nothing about which case stalled or why.

REQUIRED: a `timeout` on each msiexec invocation, and a timed-out case REPORTED as a case outcome with its own reason, not collapsed into a crash. The harness already distinguishes exit 1 (a real case failure) from exit 2 (a refusal over arguments or platform) precisely so a configuration mistake is not filed as a product defect; a stall is a third thing and must not be filed as either.

REQUIRED: the bound is per-invocation and derived. A silent install of this MSI is seconds of work.

REQUIRED: a timed-out case is NEVER recorded as pass, and never as not-run with a reason that reads like a deliberate skip -- F2's `not-run` means 'the evidence does not exist', and a stall means 'we did not find out'.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what any case does, and the step-level bound PL-0736 added, which stays as the outer limit.
assigned.notes: P2 rather than P1 because the outer bound now exists, so the failure mode is 'the step dies at 15 minutes with a poor message' rather than 'the job burns an hour'. It is still a real defect: the message is what a person reads at 2am.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs: 42 tests, 42 pass (was 33; this task adds 9). Full npm run test:scripts: green, rc=0. repo:validate: passed.

TWO CASES RUN A REAL CHILD RATHER THAN ASSERTING A BELIEF ABOUT spawnSync. The whole repair rests on Node's timeout semantics, so they are exercised: a child that sleeps 60s with timeout 250 returns status null and error.code ETIMEDOUT; a missing binary returns status null and error.code ENOENT. THAT PAIR IS THE DEFECT -- the old code tested status !== 0, so a stall and an absent msiexec.exe both arrived as a bare fail with status: null and nothing to read.

MUTATION-TESTED, five ways this repair could be undone:
  no-timeout        (delete timeout from the spawn options)   -> 1 test fails
  stall-is-notrun   (a stall recorded as not-run)             -> 2 tests fail
  gate-off          (jobFailed returns false)                 -> 2 tests fail
  spawn-as-stall    (a spawn failure dressed as a timeout)    -> 1 test fails
  timeout-too-long  (180s -> 300s)                            -> 1 test fails

The first and last are the ones worth naming. no-timeout is the mutant every other case in this block would survive, because they drive classifyInvocation with synthetic results and would keep passing while timedOut quietly never became true again on a machine nobody in this container can run; it is caught only because the spawn options are a frozen exported value with an assertion on them. timeout-too-long is caught because the step bound arithmetic is ASSERTED rather than left in a comment: four invocations at 300s is 20 minutes against PL-0736's 15-minute timeout-minutes, so the step would die with no report and the deadline would have bought nothing.

NOT CLAIMED: nothing here runs msiexec, and no Windows machine was involved. What is tested is the decision -- what an invocation means -- which is the same division the rest of this harness keeps between residue.mjs deciding and msiexec measuring.

assigned.title: desktop-shell-ci.yml is the one workflow with no timeout at all
assigned.acceptance:
FOUND BY PL-0736, OUTSIDE ITS SURFACE. That task's acceptance names `ci.yml` and `windows.yml` and its allowedPaths hold exactly those two, so this file was not touched -- but the audit that produced the bounds read every workflow, and `windows-shell` is now the only job in this repository with no `timeout-minutes`, job-level or step-level.

Its shape is the one most likely to stall: `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`, a Swatinem cache restore, and `cargo test`/`clippy`/`build --release` on a Windows runner, all of which reach the network and the first of which is the single slowest minute this repository spends.

REQUIRED: a job bound derived from an observed duration, with the derivation written beside it, in the same form `ci.yml` now uses.

REQUIRED: generous. A Windows Rust release build on a cold cache is genuinely long, and a bound that fires on one teaches people to re-run rather than to read.

OUT OF SCOPE: anything the job does, and the new `experiment-1a.yml`, which was written with `timeout-minutes: 45` already on it.
assigned.notes: P3 because this job is not on the release path -- `windows.yml` is what produces installers -- and because a six-hour stall here is visible as an unfinished run rather than as a wrong answer. Recorded now so it is written down rather than remembered.

assigned.title: The desktop shell cannot load its own user interface: every page load is refused 403
assigned.acceptance:
THE DEFECT, ESTABLISHED BY READING THE CODE AND NOT BY INFERENCE. The shipped Windows shell navigates its webview to the sidecar's loopback origin and that request is REFUSED with 403 and no body, so the application window shows nothing. Four links, each verified:
  1. apps/web/src/proxy.ts calls authorizeRequest(...) on every matched request and returns `new NextResponse(null, { status: 403 })` when it refuses.
  2. apps/web/src/lib/sidecar/policy.ts's authorizeRequest returns `refused` when `presented === null`. It is active whenever isSidecarMode is true, and isSidecarMode is `environment.token !== null` -- which the shell always satisfies, because supplying the token is how it launches the sidecar.
  3. proxy.ts's matcher is ["/((?!_next/static|favicon\\.ico).*)"]. It excludes immutable static output and NOTHING ELSE, so the document request for `/` is matched. The comment above it says the exclusion exists so the token is not 'a prerequisite for the browser to load the page that presents it' -- which is exactly the problem for the page itself.
  4. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/windows_host.rs's show_window calls `window.navigate(url)`. That is a plain top-level navigation and carries no custom headers.

NOTHING IN THE REPOSITORY SETS x-liberty-sidecar-token ON A WEBVIEW REQUEST. The only non-test producer is apps/desktop/sidecar-bootstrap/acceptance.mjs, a manual harness that drives the sidecar over HTTP without a webview. The shell has never been run end to end against a live sidecar because PW-0504 (installed-application qualification) is BLOCKED on the commander's hardware, which is why a defect this total has survived.

REQUIRED: THE SHELL PRESENTS THE TOKEN, AND THE GUARD IS NOT WEAKENED. Use WebView2's own request interception -- ICoreWebView2::AddWebResourceRequestedFilter plus add_WebResourceRequested -- and set the header on the intercepted request. The shell already owns the token; this is the shell presenting a credential it minted, which is what the handshake was always for.

REQUIRED: THE FILTER IS SCOPED TO THE SIDECAR'S EXACT ORIGIN, and this is the security-relevant line of the whole change. The token must be attached to requests to the loopback origin the handshake reported and to NOTHING ELSE. A filter of "*" would send a per-launch secret to every host the webview ever reaches. The origin comes from the parsed handshake, never from a guess, and the filter is built from it.

REQUIRED: THE ORDER IS ASSERTABLE. Installing the interceptor must happen BEFORE navigation, because a filter added after the document request has been issued does not apply to it. ShellHost gains a step for it so shell.rs's existing ordering tests can assert it, in the same style as `the_job_exists_before_the_child_and_the_child_is_assigned_before_anything_else`. An ordering that is only true by line position in windows_host.rs is not a tested property.

REQUIRED: THE TOKEN IS NEVER LOGGED, NEVER PUT IN A URL, AND NEVER WIDENS THE PROXY. No query parameter, no fragment, no cookie bootstrap, no exemption added to proxy.ts's matcher, no change to authorizeRequest. sidecar.rs's existing test `the_error_display_never_repeats_the_token` and sidecar_log.rs's redaction set the standard and the new code must meet it: a test must assert the token does not appear in any Debug or Display output this change adds.

REQUIRED: A FAILURE TO INSTALL THE INTERCEPTOR IS A STARTUP FAILURE, NOT A SILENT ONE. If the webview cannot be reached or the filter cannot be added, the window would open on a 403 with no explanation -- the exact state this task exists to end. It must route through the existing StartupFailure/FailureReport path so the commander sees a sentence instead of a blank window.

MUST NOT: weaken, bypass or special-case the request guard. Not by exempting document requests, not by making the token optional for loopback, not by widening the matcher. gpt-architect's round-95 ruling against silent downgrades applies directly, and policy.ts cites it by name.

MUST NOT: touch the player, mpv, DirectComposition or the composition-hosting question. That is PL-0752's subject and the integration route is a D1 decision with gpt-architect.

MUST NOT: claim the desktop application now works. This removes one total blocker on the first step of launching it. Whether the UI then renders, whether playback works and whether anything else is broken downstream are all unobserved, and PW-0504 is still the only thing that can establish them.
assigned.notes: FILED 2026-10-10 during Wave 9 reconnaissance, while establishing whether the proven Experiment 1c architecture could be integrated. It cannot yet -- that is blocked on a D1 decision about wry -- but this was found on the way and it is upstream of all player work: no player integration matters while the window cannot load the page. Requires security-review because the change moves a per-launch secret onto an intercepted request path, and the scoping of that interception is the only thing keeping it off other origins.

build.evidence:
BUILD: cargo check and cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -D warnings, clean for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc AND for the host. UNIT: cargo test --locked, 66 passed, 0 failed -- 62 before this change plus the 4 it adds. repo:validate passed.

THE DEFECT THIS FIXES, and it is total rather than partial: the shipped Windows shell could not load its own user interface. Four links, each read rather than inferred. apps/web/src/proxy.ts calls authorizeRequest on every matched request and answers a refusal with 403 and no body. apps/web/src/lib/sidecar/policy.ts refuses when presentedToken === null, and isSidecarMode is `environment.token !== null`, which the shell always satisfies because supplying the token is how it launches the sidecar. proxy.ts's matcher excludes only _next/static and favicon.ico, so the DOCUMENT request is matched -- and the comment above that matcher says the exclusion exists so the token is not "a prerequisite for the browser to load the page that presents it", which is precisely the problem for the page itself. And windows_host.rs's show_window loads the page with window.navigate(url), a plain top-level navigation carrying no headers. Nothing in the repository sets x-liberty-sidecar-token on a webview request; the only non-test producer is apps/desktop/sidecar-bootstrap/acceptance.mjs, a manual HTTP harness with no webview. It survived because PW-0504 is BLOCKED on the commander's hardware and the shell has never been run end to end against a live sidecar.

THE FIX DOES NOT WEAKEN THE GUARD, which was the one thing it could not do. No exemption in proxy.ts, no change to authorizeRequest, no optional-token path for loopback, no cookie bootstrap and nothing in a URL. The shell presents the credential it already minted, on requests it can see, through WebView2's own interception: ICoreWebView2::AddWebResourceRequestedFilter plus add_WebResourceRequested, with the handler calling ICoreWebView2HttpRequestHeaders::SetHeader. Three alternatives were considered and rejected in the source: a query parameter puts a per-launch secret in a URL and in every log that records one; a cookie cannot be set before the first request, which is the refused one; exempting document requests weakens the guard for every caller rather than for this one.

TWO LAYERS OF SCOPING, AND THE SECOND IS NOT REDUNDANT. The filter is "{origin}/*" where origin comes from the CHILD's handshake -- handshake::parse has already refused any host that is not a loopback literal -- and never a wildcard, because a filter matching every URL would hand a per-launch secret to every host the webview ever reached. Inside the handler the request's own URI is re-checked against the same origin prefix before the header is set, and a non-matching request is passed through UNTOUCHED rather than refused, because refusing other origins is not this handler's job. The wildcard semantics of the filter are Microsoft's rather than ours; a credential is worth one string comparison per request to be sure of where it is going.

THE ORDER IS A TESTED PROPERTY, NOT A LINE POSITION. Request interception applies to requests issued after it is installed, so an interceptor added after the navigation does not cover the document request it was added for. ShellHost therefore gains authorize_webview(&origin, &token) and start_once calls it immediately before show_window, which the Fake records like every other call -- the same discipline as the_job_exists_before_the_child_and_the_child_is_assigned_before_anything_else. An ordering true only by statement order inside windows_host.rs, which by design has no tests, would not have been a property at all.

AND IT IS SYNCHRONOUS FROM THE SHELL THREAD ON PURPOSE. with_webview dispatches to the thread owning the webview while this runs on the thread lib.rs spawned, so the outcome returns over an mpsc channel with a 10-second timeout. Without that this would return Ok before the filter existed and the ordering guarantee would be a comment. A wedged event loop becomes a startup failure with a sentence in it rather than a shell that never returns.

A FAILURE IS A STARTUP FAILURE. Carrying on would open the window on a 403 with no body, which to a user is indistinguishable from the application being broken and is the exact state this step exists to end. The child is killed and the existing StartupFailure/FailureReport path surfaces a sentence.

FOUR NEW TESTS, and each asserts a different property: the_webview_is_authorized_before_it_is_pointed_at_anything (ordering); the_webview_is_authorized_for_the_origin_the_child_reported_and_with_the_minted_token (the origin is the handshake's and the token is the mint's, and the same origin is the one navigated to, so the authorization cannot be scoped somewhere the navigation does not go); a_webview_that_cannot_be_authorized_refuses_to_start_rather_than_showing_a_refusal (no window, child killed, failure surfaced); and the_token_still_never_reaches_the_spawn_arguments_now_that_a_method_takes_one, which sweeps every recorded call and asserts the token is absent from argv, from paths, from the navigated URL and from any user-visible message -- while asserting POSITIVELY that it IS in the child's environment, so a silent removal fails too.

SIX MUTANTS, ALL CAUGHT: authorizing after the navigation instead of before; authorizing a hardcoded origin instead of the reported one; authorizing with a different token; ignoring an authorize failure and showing the window anyway; removing the step entirely; and appending the token to the navigated URL. All six reverted, 66/66 green afterwards.

THE WINDOWS-ONLY CODE IS REALLY COMPILED, proved rather than assumed: a deliberate type error inside install_token_header produced errors naming src/windows_host.rs:131 for the Windows target, then reverted. That function is unreachable from a host-target build.

ONE CORRECTNESS DETAIL WORTH RECORDING. ICoreWebView2WebResourceRequest::Uri writes into an out-parameter the CALLER owns. webview2-com offers take_pwstr, which reads and then frees with CoTaskMemFree, and string_from_pcwstr, which only reads. The handler runs on every request the page makes, so using the reading-only helper would leak a string per request; take_pwstr is used and the reason is in the source.

THE LOCKFILE MOVED BY EXACTLY TWO LINES, both dependency edges: "webview2-com" and "windows" were added to liberty-desktop's dependency list. A package-by-package comparison reports moved: none, added: none, removed: none, 417 entries before and after. Both were already resolved at these exact versions as tauri 2.12.0's own dependencies, so --locked is honoured.

NOT FORMATTED, AND SAID RATHER THAN QUIETLY DONE. cargo fmt --check is dirty for TEN files in this crate including seven I did not touch, so the crate has never been rustfmt-clean and desktop-shell-ci.yml does not check it. Running cargo fmt would have produced a large reformatting diff unrelated to this defect. The two files I changed are left in the crate's existing style.

NOT CLAIMED: that the desktop application now works. This removes ONE total blocker on the first step of launching it. Whether the UI then renders, whether anything is broken downstream, and whether the installed build behaves are all unobserved -- PW-0504 on the commander's hardware is the only thing that can establish them, and it is still BLOCKED. No PW-0504 row is marked passed. The player is untouched: no mpv, no DirectComposition, no composition hosting, and the integration route for Experiment 1c remains a D1 decision with gpt-architect.

unit.evidence: cargo test --locked: 66 passed, 0 failed. 62 before this change, 4 added. The four: the_webview_is_authorized_before_it_is_pointed_at_anything; the_webview_is_authorized_for_the_origin_the_child_reported_and_with_the_minted_token; a_webview_that_cannot_be_authorized_refuses_to_start_rather_than_showing_a_refusal; the_token_still_never_reaches_the_spawn_arguments_now_that_a_method_takes_one. Six mutants all caught -- see the build gate for the list. The full reasoning, the scoping argument and what is NOT claimed are in the build gate evidence on this task; it is not repeated here.
